_comment: ❌️ The refusal corpus. Every input MUST fail, and MUST fail with exactly `message` — the verbatim text the CLI prints. `mutation` marks the inputs the second scenario replays to prove a refusal leaves no trace: no event, no changed record.

refusals.boundary: A field the query root does not carry is named, not ignored.

refusals.message: graphql errors: [tickets: unknown field "nope" on Ticket]
refusals.boundary: A nested refusal is wrapped in the `field: cause` chain that says where it happened.

refusals.message: graphql errors: [tickets: dates: unknown field "nope" on TicketDate]
refusals.boundary: The chain nests as deep as the selection does.
The two roots are separate field tables; a mutation is not reachable from a query.
The mutation root refuses the same way the query root does.
A document the grammar cannot read never reaches a resolver.

refusals.message: graphql errors: [node: invalid node id format: garbage]
refusals.boundary: An id in no recognised shape is refused rather than answered with null.

refusals.source: mutation { ticketClose(input: { year: 2026, month: 9, day: 6, slug: "NO-SUCH-TICKET", summary: "never" }) { status } }
refusals.boundary: A write against an aggregate that does not exist refuses instead of inventing one.

refusals.message: graphql errors: [goalChange: goal no-such-goal not found]
refusals.boundary: The same rule holds for every aggregate, not only for tickets.

refusals.message: graphql errors: [folderMove: folder nowhere not found]
refusals.boundary: A move names its source; an absent source is a refusal, not a create.

refusals.source: mutation { ticketReopen(input: { year: 1999, month: 1, day: 1, slug: "NOPE", prompt: "p", client: CODEX, llm: "gpt" }) { status } }
refusals.boundary: A reopen is a write like any other and refuses on the same terms.
